content: The medication sodium/potassium/magnesium sulfate solution is used to cleanse the intestines prior to a colonoscopy. It functions as a laxative by drawing significant amounts of water into the colon, resulting in watery bowel movements. Before using this product, carefully read the Medication Guide and Instructions for Use provided by your pharmacist. Follow any specific dietary instructions given by your doctor. Typically, you may have a light breakfast or consume only clear liquids the day before your procedure. After breakfast, you should only drink clear liquids until after the procedure. Avoid milk, alcoholic beverages, or any food or drink that is red or purple in color. Do not take any other oral medications within one hour of starting the solution. This product is usually taken in two doses: one in the evening before the colonoscopy and the second dose the following morning. To prepare the solution, pour the contents into the provided mixing container as directed, add cool water, mix thoroughly, and drink the entire mixture. After consuming the solution, drink two additional containers of water over the next hour. Watery bowel movements typically begin about one hour after drinking the solution. Watery bowel movements are an expected effect of this medication. Other possible side effects include nausea, vomiting, bloating, or abdominal cramping. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. However, it can cause dehydration or electrolyte imbalances if your body loses too much fluid and salts. Serious allergic reactions to this medication are rare. If you experience severe symptoms such as fainting or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. For other concerns, contact your doctor or a poison control center. In the U.S., you can call 1-800-222-1222 for poison control assistance. Before taking this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you have any allergies, as this product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used if clearly necessary, and it is unknown if it passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. If you are unable to drink the entire solution and water as directed, contact your doctor immediately. Store the unmixed container at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
